name: Netflix Sign In
description: A 'Who's watching?' profile gate. Pick a face and it arcs to the centre of the screen and grows — one node the whole way, on Motion's own `arc()` path — while the other four close the gap behind it. A four-box PIN pad unfolds downward out of the face before it has even landed. A wrong PIN shakes and clears; the right one crossfades the roster out, a tab bar in, and flies the face down into the Profile tab, all on one clock. Escape or Back sends it home along a different arc than it left on.

variations.name: default
variations.previewHint: Pick a face, then type its PIN from the margin note — try a wrong one first for the shake. Pass profiles without a pin to see an unlocked one go straight through
variations.description: A profile-picker gate where the chosen avatar flies on an `arc()` path between the roster and the centre, a PIN pad grows out of it, and success hands the bottom of the screen over to a tab bar the face lands in.

props.name: profiles
props.description: The roster. Defaults to five drawn faces (Ari, Nova, Pip, Wren, Bo) with PINs 1234, 2580, 1379, 4321, 0000. Five fit a 340px-wide host; more need a wider one.

props.name: profiles[].name
props.description: Label under the face. Also interpolated into the PIN label and the Profile tab's accessible name.

props.name: profiles[].pin
props.description: The answer the default verifier compares against. A profile with no pin is unlocked: pick it and it flies, pauses, and signs in with no pad.

props.name: profiles[].locked
props.description: Whether the gate asks for a PIN at all. Defaults to pin !== undefined, so set it only when the answer lives on a server and you are passing onVerify.

props.name: profiles[].color
props.description: Ground colour of the avatar box and of the glow it throws on the screen while it is up. Defaults to the drawn face's own colour, cycled by index.

props.name: profiles[].avatar
props.description: Replaces the drawn face. An is sized to fill the box. Rendered at avatarSize and scaled up 2.19× in flight, never resized — keep it vector or well above 110px.

props.name: tabs
props.description: The tabs after Profile in the signed-in bar. Profile is always first: it is the landing pad the face flies into. Defaults to Search and Downloads.

props.name: tabs[].name
props.description: Tab label.

props.name: tabs[].icon
props.description: HugeIcons icon component rendered in the tab's box.

props.name: tabs[].onClick
props.description: Click handler for the tab.

props.name: onVerify
props.type: (pin: string, profile: Profile, index: number) => boolean | Promise<boolean>
props.description: Decides whether a PIN is right. Replaces the default local comparison (which waits 900ms to stand in for a round trip). The pad stays locked until it resolves; a false, a rejection or a throw all count as wrong. A result that arrives after Back or a new pick is ignored.

props.name: onSignIn
props.description: Fires when the face lands in the Profile tab — the end of the flow.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Fires when Back or Escape has returned the face to the row.

props.name: heading
props.description: Defaults to "Who’s watching?".

props.name: pinLabel
props.description: Label above the boxes. A function because the name is interpolated. Defaults to `Enter ${name}’s PIN`.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Shown under the boxes on a wrong PIN. Defaults to "That PIN doesn’t match.".

props.name: welcome
props.description: The greeting that takes the face's place on success. Defaults to "Welcome back!" / "Enjoy your weekend.". Omit subtitle to show the title alone.

props.name: backLabel
props.description: Defaults to "← Back". Escape does the same thing.

props.name: profileTabLabel
props.description: Label under the landing tab. Defaults to "Profile".

props.name: showHint
props.description: Draws the dashed margin note that leaks the chosen profile's PIN. Demo scaffolding: the preview passes it, an installed block should not. Defaults to false, and never draws for a profile without a pin.

props.name: pinLength
props.description: Number of PIN boxes. The last one submits by itself. Defaults to 4.

props.name: avatarSize
props.description: Face size in the row, in px. Radius, focus-ring offset and the grown size all derive from it. Defaults to 50.

props.name: className
props.description: Appended to the screen's classes. The block fills its container; the phone frame in the preview is host chrome, not part of the block.

features: Takes the roster, tabs, every line of copy and an async `onVerify` as props — a profile with no `pin` is unlocked and skips the pad, and a late verification result is ignored once the gate has moved on

Flies the picked face on Motion's `arc()` handed to `transition.path` — x and y get nothing but a destination, the path bends the line, and `rotate: 0.5` makes the lean follow the tangent instead of a hand-kept keyframe
Keeps it one node the whole way: a hand-measured FLIP against the stage, with the roster slot going invisible but never unmounting so the row has a rectangle to fly back to

Takes a different road home for free — `direction: "cw"` is locked to the direction of travel, so the same setting bulges to the opposite side once the journey reverses; a retraced path reads as a rewind
Stacks three nested scales that multiply — the journey, an anticipation dip (1 → 0.86 → 1 tween), and a 0.34-bounce growth spring delayed 70ms — so the tap is its own beat under the climb
Unfolds the PIN pad downward out of the face from a top-edge transform origin, timed as a FRACTION of the flight (enters at 80% of the ascent, gone by 20% of the descent) so retiming one retimes both
Uses four decorative boxes over ONE real input — paste, backspace, mobile keyboards and screen readers all work — with the caret and digits popping in on a 0.42-bounce spring

Shakes imperatively via `useAnimationControls` so the same wrong PIN twice in a row still fires, and hands the whole bottom of the screen over on one `barFade` clock when the PIN is right: roster out, tab bar in, face down into the Profile tab
Mounts the tab bar from frame one at opacity 0 so the Profile tab has a rectangle to aim the descent at in the same commit the fade begins
Under reduced motion the arc is dropped entirely — the traveller cross-dissolves between its two rectangles and the row fades without moving

featureSections.title: The Flight
featureSections.summary: One avatar node arcs between the roster and the centre on a real `arc()` path, measured against the stage rather than the viewport.
points: Two module-scope `arc()` instances, one per leg, so the continuity closure that keeps an interrupted flight from snapping is never rebuilt
Seeds x/y motion values at the departing slot before the ascent, but never before the descent — an interrupted climb turns round from wherever it is
Drives the leg imperatively with `useAnimationControls`: a change to the path changes the transition, not the destination, and a declarative target would not replay
Out leg peaks early (0.21) and leans hard (0.5); home leg is symmetric and flatter, quicker and bouncier on the shrink because going home is not a decision

featureSections.title: The Row
featureSections.summary: The other four faces are part of the flight, not bystanders to it.
points: Removes the picked face from the list and lets AnimatePresence popLayout pull it out of flow on frame one, so the gap closes while the traveller is still climbing
Re-inserts it at opacity 0 the moment the descent STARTS, so the row makes space before the face lands rather than reacting afterwards
Runs the row's layout animation on exactly the leg's duration and ease, so gap and face are one movement
No exit animation on the leaving item — two copies of one face crossfading past each other would give the trick away

featureSections.title: The PIN Pad
featureSections.summary: Four boxes, one input, and a pad that grows out of the avatar instead of arriving beside it.
points: Unfolds from `transformOrigin: top center` directly under the grown face, 2px below it, on a spring delayed to 80% of the ascent
One numeric `<input>` with `autoComplete="one-time-code"`, labelled by the visible text via aria-labelledby, described by the error via aria-describedby
Focus ring is an `outline`, not a Tailwind ring — box-shadows vanish in forced-colors mode — and it lands only on the box the next keypress fills
The fourth digit submits by itself; a wrong PIN shakes the pad wrapper (never the traveller, whose x is owned by the flight), clears, and announces politely with an alert glyph beside the message
The verdict lands on the boxes themselves: green tint and ink while the face is being let through, red on a wrong PIN — two values of one treatment

featureSections.title: Signing In
featureSections.summary: Success is one event with one clock, not three things given the same number.
points: A correct PIN measures the Profile tab's centre, flips `signedIn`, and starts the descent in a single commit
Roster fades out, tab bar fades in, greeting fades in, glow fades out — all on `barFade`, which is the descent's own duration
The pad exits on `easeIn` within the first fifth of the descent, so the face travels home over an empty stage
Landing in the tab is instant, not a fade: the traveller unmounts in the same frame the Profile tab's avatar appears
